name: Gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumors
theme: the slow cancer with a clock of its own · grade routes everything

meta.title: GI neuroendocrine tumors in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors of the GI tract (pancreatic NET is its own queued trainer)
meta.population: Adults with well-differentiated GI neuroendocrine tumors - THE SLOW CANCER WITH A CLOCK OF ITS OWN: incidence up 6.4-fold since 1973 (Dasari VERIFIED: 1.09 to 6.98 per 100,000; 20-year prevalence 171,321 - more prevalent than esophageal, gastric, and pancreatic adenocarcinoma COMBINED, and exactly that comparison, verified). GRADE ROUTES EVERYTHING - and the WHO 2019 lesson ships verified: G3-NET and NEC share the SAME Ki-67 cutoff (>20%) - the discriminator is DIFFERENTIATION (morphology + molecular: MEN1/DAXX/ATRX vs TP53/RB1), never Ki-67 alone; 'carcinoid' is retired from the digestive classification and survives only in the lung and in the syndrome names. THE BORDERS ARE FOUR: pancreatic NET blocks to its own queued trainer (sunitinib's pNET-only label is the border's regulatory receipt, verified); poorly differentiated NEC blocks as a different disease (platinum-etoposide convention); appendiceal NET reroutes LIVE to the appendiceal trainer (the registry's SEVENTEENTH live reroute - with the ENETS 2023 rule shift noted: appendectomy adequate <=2cm absent risk factors); and the SEER re-anchor is a correction of this run's own briefing: small-bowel NET 5-yr OS ~69% overall, localized 65-71%, distant 36-54% - the rosier grade-stratified figures survive only with the referral-center hedge printed.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the slow cancer with a clock of its own. THE VERIFIED FOUNDATION: PROMID (octreotide - time to progression 14.3 vs 6 months, HR 0.34, verified verbatim - and the ENDPOINT TRAP documented: TTP, not PFS) and CLARINET (lanreotide - PFS HR 0.47, median not-reached vs 18 months, verified) make somatostatin analogs the first move in advanced G1-G2 disease. THE PRRT ARC ships with every number verified: NETTER-1 (progressive midgut post-SSA: PFS HR 0.21; ORR 18.8% vs 3.0%; approved 2018-01-26) INCLUDING its honest ending - final OS 48.0 vs 36.3 months NOT sta…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO 2019/2022 digestive NEN (verified receipt): well-differentiated NET G1 (Ki-67 <3%) / G2 (3-20%) / G3 (>20%) vs poorly differentiated NEC - morphology-first distinction; profile router = localized / advanced G1-G2 / advanced G3-NET; SSTR status as the PRRT gate (Krenning-level uptake, DOTATATE PET era); functional status (carcinoid syndrome) as its own care layer
meta.response: Cross-sectional + SSTR imaging response conventions; chromogranin/5-HIAA as adjuncts (never routers); the years-long clock acknowledged in every horizon

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A disease of the sixties on average - and one where the years-long clock makes fitness-for-sequence matter more than fitness-for-one-drug.
Patient.helpPatient: This cancer is usually found in middle age or later - and plans are built for years, not months.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Most of this menu is gentle (depot injections, oral targeted agents); the exceptions - PRRT logistics, liver procedures, G3 chemotherapy - are where fitness gates.
Patient.helpPatient: Much of this treatment is gentler than classic chemotherapy - strength matters most for procedures.

Disease.helpPatient: Neuroendocrine tumors from different organs - and their aggressive poorly-differentiated cousins - follow different playbooks; the pathology report and primary site decide which trainer applies.

Disease.help: GRADE ROUTES EVERYTHING: localized disease runs the surgical chapter (with the adjuvant desert said - no randomized evidence, surveillance only); advanced G1-G2 runs the SSA-first foundation with the…
Disease.helpPatient: How far the tumor has spread and how fast its cells divide (the grade) together pick the chapter - from surgery-only through gentle injections to chemotherapy.

Disease.help: The PRRT gate is OPERATIONAL: NETTER-1/-2 required tumor uptake at least equal to liver (Krenning-level) - a DOTATATE-cold tumor gets no radioligand card. The scan itself is the modern standard (Sado…
Disease.helpPatient: A special scan shows whether the tumor carries the docking site the radioactive treatment needs - bright scan, open door.

Disease.helpPatient: If the tumor makes hormones (flushing, diarrhea), that gets its own treatments - and the heart valves deserve a periodic check.

On treatment.label: Course read
On treatment.help: STABILITY IS SUCCESS in this disease - the SSA trials were won on delaying progression, not shrinking tumors. Progression routes to the receipted shelf: PRRT (if SSTR-positive), everolimus, cabozanti…
On treatment.helpPatient: In this slow cancer, 'no change' on scans is genuinely good news - and if it does grow, several proven next steps exist.

Newly diagnosed.name: Resection + surveillance (localized - and the adjuvant desert said)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: surgical + endoscopic conventions (ENETS/NANETS secondhand); SEER anchors
Newly diagnosed.evidence: convention + SEER-verified anchors; no adjuvant evidence (desert)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: operative/endoscopic risk only - no adjuvant therapy exists to add toxicity
Newly diagnosed.patient: For localized disease: an operation (or for small rectal/stomach tumors, an endoscopic removal) - and then watching, because no add-on drug has ever been shown to help after complete removal.
drugs: Site-appropriate resection (segmental bowel + mesenteric clearance / endoscopic by size rules) + surveillance

Newly diagnosed.name: Somatostatin analog first (advanced G1-G2 - the verified foundation)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: 1L standard for advanced G1-G2 (PROMID + CLARINET verified)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: among oncology's gentlest ledgers - injection-site, gallstones, glucose shifts
Newly diagnosed.patient: A monthly injection - often the entire first treatment - proven in two randomized trials to hold this slow cancer still, sometimes for years.

Newly diagnosed.name: PRRT pathway (177Lu-DOTATATE - SSTR-gated; the arc with its honest ending)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: PRRT standard (NETTER-1 verified; NETTER-2 first-line high-G2/G3 verified with label truth)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 verified-snippet x2 (OS ending taught honestly)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias, renal protection craft (amino-acid co-infusion), rare MDS/AML tail - the radioligand ledger
Newly diagnosed.patient: A targeted radioactive infusion that homes to the tumor's docking sites - four treatments over eight months, for tumors that light up on the special scan.

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemotherapy conventions (advanced well-diff G3-NET - EA2142's null taught)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: G3-NET conventions with the randomized null taught (EA2142)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: real chemotherapy ledgers - CAPTEM gentler, EP harder
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the fastest-dividing well-differentiated tumors: real chemotherapy - two regimens were compared head-to-head and neither clearly won, so the choice weighs side effects and logistics.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.patient: Comfort-focused care is a real choice at every step - and in this disease it can be a years-long chapter, often with the hormone-controlling injection continuing.
drugs: Palliative care partnership (SSA often continued for symptom control)

Relapsed / recurrent.name: The post-SSA shelf (PRRT / everolimus / cabozantinib - all receipted)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: post-SSA standards (NETTER-1 + RADIANT-4 + CABINET all verified)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: three randomized receipts (verified); sequence evidence absent (said)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: regimen-dependent: radioligand ledger / mTOR ledger (stomatitis, pneumonitis, glucose) / TKI ledger (hypertension, fatigue, hand-foot)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the monthly injection stops holding: three proven paths - the targeted radioactive infusion (if the scan is bright), or one of two daily targeted pills, including the newest approval from 2025.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: The liver chapter (debulking receipts + RETNET's randomized answer)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: liver-directed conventions + one randomized modality receipt (RETNET)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: surgical-series receipts + randomized phase 2 (secondhand); selection said
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: post-embolization syndrome; operative risk; the carcinoid-crisis correction applies in every procedure suite
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the liver carries most of the disease: surgery to remove the bulk of it, or blocking its blood supply through a catheter - real options at experienced centers, with a randomized trial guiding the catheter choice.
drugs: Hepatic debulking surgery and/or trans-arterial embolization (TAE/cTACE - RETNET-informed)

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort-focused care is a real choice at every step.

refs.label: THE WHO 2019 DISCIPLINE, verified: 'What is New in the 2019 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Digestive System...' (PMID 32233993, pubmed-url-match): well-diff NET G1 (<3%) / G2 (3-20%) / G3 (>20%) split from poorly diff NEC - G3-NET and NEC share the SAME Ki-67 cutoff; the discriminator is DIFFERENTIATION (morphology + molecular: MEN1/DAXX/ATRX vs TP53/RB1). 'Carcinoid' retired from digestive classification (kept in lung + syndrome names - memory-grade). Platinum-etoposide for NEC = NORDIC-derived convention (memory-grade); Ki-67>55% as platinum-response marker = convention, memory-grade | PMID 32233993 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

EPI, verified-snippet: Dasari (JAMA Oncol 2017 - PMID 28448665, pubmed-url-match): incidence 1.09 (1973) -> 6.98/100,000 (2012); 64,971 cases; GEP 3.56/100,000; 20-yr prevalence 171,321 - MORE THAN esophageal (~36,857) + gastric (~79,843) + pancreatic adenocarcinoma (~49,620) COMBINED (exactly that comparison - never 'most GI cancers')

PROMID, verified-snippet (Rinke, JCO 2009 - PMID 19704057, pubmed-url-match): octreotide LAR in midgut NET - median TIME TO PROGRESSION 14.3 vs 6 months (HR 0.34 [0.20-0.59], p=0.000072); SD at 6mo 66.7% vs 37.2%. THE ENDPOINT TRAP documented: TTP, not PFS - and never transplant CLARINET's 0.47 here | PMID 19704057 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

CLARINET, verified-snippet (Caplin, NEJM 2014 - PMID 25014687, pubmed-url-match: 'Lanreotide in Metastatic Enteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors'): PFS HR 0.47 (0.30-0.73); median not-reached vs 18.0 months; Ki-67<10% eligibility (methods, memory-grade) | PMID 25014687 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

NETTER-1, verified end to end: primary (NEJM 2017 - PMID 28076709, pubmed-url-match): progressive midgut post-SSA - PFS HR 0.21 (0.13-0.34); ORR 18.8% vs 3.0% (FDA evaluable set; NEJM rounds 18/3 - the TWO-FORMS note); FDA approved 2018-01-26 (verified). FINAL OS (Lancet Oncol 2021 - 34793718, matched): 48.0 vs 36.3 months - the 11.7-month difference NOT statistically significant; 36% control-arm crossover named as confounder (verified snippets - the honest ending taught). Control-arm PFS appears as 8.4 (FDA) and 8.5 (summaries) - trap noted | PMID 28076709 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25
refs.src: NEJM + Lancet Oncol + FDA (matched; ending honest)

refs.label: NETTER-2, verified numbers + corrected label story (29th): first-line Ki-67 10-55% GEP-NET (Lancet 2024, Singh - journal-URL verified; bare PubMed URL not surfaced): PFS 22.8 vs 8.5 months, stratified HR 0.276 (0.182-0.418), p<0.0001; n=226, ages >=15. THE CORRECTION: NO US label expansion followed - the 2018-01-26 label was ALREADY line- and site-agnostic ('SSTR-positive GEP-NETs including foregut, midgut, hindgut'); the 2024-04-23 expansion was PEDIATRIC >=12 via NETTER-P; NETTER-2 supported an EU filing - WITHDRAWN by the sponsor 2025-05-09 (EMA procedure II/0052; withdrawal Q&A published; EU label remains progressive G1/G2 only - refresh 2026-08-20). THE DISCRIMINATOR: the Ki-67>=10 floor means low-G2 (3-10%) first-line PRRT remains extrapolation - said | PMID 38851203 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

RADIANT-4, verified-snippet (Yao, Lancet 2016 - PMID 26703889, pubmed-url-match): everolimus in NON-FUNCTIONAL GI/lung NET - PFS 11.0 (9.2-13.3) vs 3.9 (3.6-7.4) months, HR 0.48 (0.35-0.67), p<0.00001; n=302. FDA approved 2016-02-26 (verified). THE SCOPE TRAP: citing it for functional midgut disease is a border error | PMID 26703889 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

CABINET - the newest card (Chan, NEJM 2024, NEJMoa2403991 - journal-URL verified; PubMed URL not surfaced): cabozantinib vs placebo, previously treated - extrapancreatic cohort (n=203) PFS 8.4 vs 3.9 months, stratified HR 0.38; positive in BOTH cohorts (pNET HR memory-grade). FDA APPROVED 2025-03-26 (adults + pediatric >=12; previously treated well-diff pNET AND epNET - 'regardless of site/grade/SSTR/functionality' framing verified). THE TWO-NUMBER-SETS TRAP documented: FDA label/BICR prints epNET 8.5 vs 4.2 and pNET 13.8 vs 3.3 - this trainer cites NEJM consistently, labeled | PMID 39282913 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

THE SYNDROME LAYER at exact grade: TELESTAR (Kulke, JCO 2017 - ascopubs mirror-verified): telotristat in SSA-refractory carcinoid diarrhea - week-12 BM reduction -0.9 placebo vs -1.7 (250mg) vs -2.1 (500mg); FDA 2017 (date memory-grade); the TELECAST sister-trial trap noted (different endpoints). Carcinoid HEART: Hedinger right-sided valvulopathy; NT-proBNP >260 ng/L -> echo (JACC 2017 expert statement, mirror-verified). THE CRISIS CORRECTION (28th), verified: prophylactic octreotide does NOT prevent intraoperative crisis (PMID 26603846, pubmed-url-match: 'does not prevent'; meta-analysis 35740631, matched; crises ~19-25% of NET operations regardless) - treat when they occur; the prophylaxis convention = contested legacy dogma, labeled | PMID 26603846 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

THE SCAN, verified with the misfiling trap: Sadowski prospective 68Ga-DOTATATE PET study = JCO 2016;34:588-596 (NOT JAMA Oncol - the trap documented): detected lesions in 65.2% of symptomatic biochemically-negative patients; 40% missed by anatomic imaging AND octreoscan SPECT; head-to-head receipt 30850506 (matched). NETSPOT (68Ga) 2016-06 / Detectnet (64Cu) 2020-09 - dates memory-grade. THE KRENNING GATE: NETTER-1/-2 required uptake >= liver - the operational PRRT criterion (convention verified via trial design) | PMID 30850506 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

SURGERY + THE HONEST NUMBERS: SEER anchors (verified via SEER-based receipts): small-bowel NET 5-yr OS ~69% overall; localized 65-71%; distant 36-54% - the CORRECTION (30th): rosier grade-stratified figures (localized G1 ~95%; metastatic G1/G2 60-70%) are referral-center claims, hedged wherever used. Debulking: the >70% cytoreduction threshold has surgical-series receipts (Graff-Baker/Pommier line; 'Effective cytoreduction' Surgery 2018 - mirror-verified; the 90% dogma lowered); NO randomized debulking-vs-not trial (desert). Small-bowel conventions: primary + mesenteric nodal clearance; multifocality palpated. THE ADJUVANT DESERT: no randomized adjuvant evidence - surveillance only (memory-grade, high-confidence, taught)
refs.src: SEER + surgical series (verified anchors + mirror receipts)

refs.label: RETNET - the modality answer (correction 33rd: the 'liver-directed desert' premise was wrong): randomized phase 2 (NCT02724540), TAE (n=78) vs cTACE (n=73) vs DEB-TACE - NO hepatic-PFS difference TAE vs cTACE; equal symptom control <=2yr; DEB-TACE arm CLOSED EARLY (40% SAE); TAE G3-4 toxicity 54% vs cTACE 36% (SIR/NANETS 2025 + JVIR - secondhand). Bland = chemo; beads abandoned. No randomized surgical-debulking trial exists (that desert stands)

GASTRIC TYPES I-III + RECTAL RULES (mirror-verified conventions): gastric type I (70-80%; atrophic-gastritis hypergastrinemia; multiple <1cm; indolent; endoscopic + lifelong surveillance) / type II (ZES/MEN1) / type III (sporadic, normogastrinemic, >2cm, metastasis risk >50% - oncologic resection); rectal: <=10mm endoscopic (mEMR/ESD), 10-20mm EUS/MRI + MDT, >=20mm radical surgery (ENETS 2023 colorectal guidance, doi 10.1111/jne.13309 - mirror)

THE GRAVEYARD: SWOG S0518, verified (PMID 28384065, pubmed-url-match: octreotide + interferon-alfa-2b vs octreotide + bevacizumab, n=427, JCO 2017) - the DOUBLE NEGATIVE taught: bevacizumab NOT superior (PFS ~16.6 vs 15.4, memory-grade numbers) - burying bev in NET while exposing interferon as real-but-toxic-superseded (never formally buried - said). IO-MONO NULL: KEYNOTE-158 NET cohort (n=107): ORR 3.7%, mPFS 4.1 (secondhand, Clin Cancer Res). DUAL-IO GRADE-RESTRICTED: DART/S1609 - 44% ORR in HIGH-grade, 0% in low/intermediate (secondhand) - active only where this trainer's disease is not | PMID 28384065 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

EA2142 - the G3 randomized null (NCT02595424, ECOG-ACRIN; ASCO 2022 - secondhand): advanced G3 non-small-cell GEP-NEN (21 G3-NET, 36 NEC), platinum-etoposide vs CAPTEM 1L - CAPTEM NOT superior (PFS 3.45 vs 5.36; OS 12.6 vs 10.6; CAPTEM less toxic) - EP remains standard, CAPTEM a tolerable option; the null taught, not spun

THE RADIOLIGAND FRONTIER + THE WATCH: ITM-11 (n.c.a. 177Lu-edotreotide) - COMPETE POSITIVE vs ACTIVE comparator (Lancet 2026-07: PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 months vs everolimus, HR 0.67, p=0.022; Gr3/4 TRAE 18% vs 40% - secondhand) and CRL 2026-08-07 (MANUFACTURING-ONLY; no clinical concern; resubmission pending - PDUFA 2026-08-28 moot) = THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY RE-CHECK; COMPOSE (NCT04919226) enrolling 1L aggressive G2/G3. ALPHA: RYZ101 ACTION-1 (NCT05477576, phase 3 post-177Lu, enrolling; ph1b ORR 29.4%); AlphaMedix 212Pb (Breakthrough 2024-02; phase 2 endpoints met ESMO 2025; ph3 NCT unverified); VMT-alpha-NET (interim ORR 43%, AACR 2026; NCT unverified); 67Cu/161Tb = pre-efficacy (desert-labeled)

THE APPENDICEAL BORDER (correction 31st + the reroute ruling): ENETS 2023 aNET guidance (PMID 37682701, pubmed-url-match): appendectomy alone adequate for most tumors <=2cm WITHOUT risk factors; hemicolectomy for >2cm/R1-R2/deep mesoappendiceal invasion - the old '1-2cm gray zone' is the 2016-era rule. BORDER RULING: appendiceal NET decisions are incidental-appendectomy pathology management sharing a differential with goblet-cell adenocarcinoma - they belong in the APPENDICEAL trainer (live reroute; the seam policed here with one pointer) | PMID 37682701 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.
